title: Chainsaw upkeep: oiler, bar, sprocket, filter, plug, fuel and cold starts
summary: Keep a chainsaw working through a winter of firewood: oil reaching the chain, a clean and square bar, a sprocket that isn't worn out, a clean filter and plug, fresh fuel mixed right, a brake that holds, and tricks for starting in the cold. The dangers are fuel spraying from a hot, pressurised tank, exhaust carbon monoxide, and cutting with a brake or chain that has stopped working.

materials.item: Bar and chain oil (a thinner grade for frost; never used motor oil)
materials.qty: A tankful each time you refuel

materials.item: Two-stroke oil for air-cooled engines (not outboard or four-stroke oil)
materials.qty: 20 mL per litre of petrol for 50:1

materials.item: Fresh petrol, no more than 10 % ethanol
materials.qty: No more than a month's worth

materials.item: Spark plug of the type named in the manual
Spare chain of the same pitch, gauge and length

steps.text: Work outdoors or in an open shed, on bare ground. Engine off and cool, chain brake on (STIHL MS 162/172); take the battery out of a battery saw (STIHL MSA 60/70) or unplug a corded one (Oregon CS1500). On a petrol saw pull the spark plug cap off too, because Husqvarna's stop switch springs back to the start position and a tug on the starter could fire the engine (Husqvarna 450 II); push it back on when you refit the plug. The muffler stays hot after the engine stops, so let the saw cool on bare ground away from dry leaves and sawdust (STIHL MS 162/172).
steps.warn: Never run or start a saw indoors: the exhaust is carbon monoxide (STIHL MS 162/172).

steps.text: Open the fuel cap slowly by hand. If fuel or vapour hisses out, close it again and let the saw cool longer (STIHL MS 162/172).
steps.warn: A hot tank, or one half full or more, can be under pressure and spray fuel when opened (STIHL MS 162/172).

steps.text: If the saw has stood a month or more with fuel in it, empty the tank into a can for disposal and start with fresh mix (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II).

Mix fresh fuel in an approved can: half the petrol, all of the two-stroke oil, shake, the rest of the petrol, shake again, then let the can sit a few minutes and open it slowly: shaking builds pressure in a fuel can (STIHL MS 162/172). At 50:1 that is 20 mL of oil per litre (Husqvarna 450 II, STIHL MS 162/172).
steps.warn: Use petrol with no more than 10 % ethanol and oil made for air-cooled two-strokes; outboard oil and four-stroke oil can damage the engine (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II).

steps.text: Take off the sprocket cover, bar and chain. Clean the oil outlet on the saw, the oil inlet hole on the bar and the bar groove with a brush or thin scraper (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II).

File off any burrs along the bar rails with a flat file. Check the groove for wear and spread, and check that a nose sprocket spins freely; grease it if it has a grease hole (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II, USFS chain saw course ch3).
steps.warn: Replace a bar with a pinched, spread or very worn groove, or soft blue heat spots (STIHL MS 162/172, USFS chain saw course ch3).

steps.text: Look at the drive sprocket and the clutch drum. STIHL replaces the sprocket when its wear marks are deeper than 0.5 mm (0.020 in). Running two chains in turn spreads the wear (STIHL MS 162/172).
Brush the wood dust and resin off the chain brake band and clutch drum, and check the front hand guard for cracks (Husqvarna 450 II).
Refit the bar turned over, so both rails wear evenly, then fit and tension the chain as in the chain guide (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II).

Take out the air filter and clean it the maker's way (Husqvarna brushes or shakes it and washes it in detergent and water; STIHL blows its filter plate out from the inside with compressed air; the Forest Service says to tap a filter clean and never use an air hose); refit it so it seals all round. Replace a damaged or worn-out filter (Husqvarna 450 II, STIHL MS 162/172).
steps.warn: Don't wash a filter in fuel (USFS chain saw course ch3).

steps.text: Take out the spark plug, clean it, check the gap (0.5 mm on the STIHL MS 162/172) and refit it firmly with the boot pressed fully on. Replace a plug with eroded electrodes (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II).
steps.warn: Use a resistor plug with a solid terminal; a loose SAE adapter tip can arc and light fuel vapour (STIHL MS 162/172).

steps.text: Brush the cooling fins and the air intake on the starter clear of dust (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II).
Fill the oil tank with bar oil, fuel the saw on bare ground with the brake on, leaving about 13 mm (1/2 in) of air space, and wipe up spills (STIHL MS 162/172).
steps.warn: Fuel at least 3 m (10 ft) from any flame or spark, OSHA's minimum for loggers; the Forest Service says 6 m (20 ft), so use 6 m where you can. Start the saw at least 3 m (10 ft) from where you fuelled it (OSHA 1910.266, USFS chain saw course ch3).

steps.text: Start the saw on the ground and test it: brake on, full throttle for no more than 3 seconds, and the chain must not move; the chain must not creep at idle; and held 20 cm (8 in) over a pale surface at three-quarter throttle it should leave a line of oil within a minute (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II).
steps.warn: A brake that slips, a chain that creeps at idle or a dry chain: stop and fix it before cutting (STIHL MS 162/172).

notes:
## What wears out
The chain, bar and drive sprocket wear as a team, and the oil supply keeps all three alive. Oregon calls the sprocket the third member of the cutting team and says a damaged one can't be repaired, only replaced (Oregon M&S manual). Filing and fitting the chain are in [Chainsaw chain](#guides/skill_chainsaw_chain); cutting fallen trees is in [Clearing a fallen tree](#guides/safety_clearing_blowdown). Fuel storage and handling are in [Fuel handling](#guides/safety_fuel_handling).

## Fuel: the mix, freshness and ethanol
- **Petrol:** STIHL certifies its MS 162/172 on 89 octane or better with no more than 10 % ethanol; Husqvarna allows 87 AKI (90 RON) or better, also up to 10 % ethanol (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II). More than 10 % ethanol causes running problems and engine damage, and switching between fuels with different ethanol levels changes the idle and top speed (STIHL MS 162/172).
- **Oil:** two-stroke oil for air-cooled engines at 50:1 (2 %). Not outboard (water-cooled, TCW) oil, not oils labelled for both water- and air-cooled engines, not four-stroke oil (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II).
- **How long it keeps:** mix no more than a month's worth: STIHL says never more than a 30-day supply, Husqvarna no more than 1 month at a time (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II). For storage of 30 days or more, STIHL drains the tank and runs the engine until it stops (STIHL MS 162/172).

| Petrol | Two-stroke oil at 50:1 |
|---|---|
| 1 L | 20 mL |
| 5 L | 100 mL |
| 10 L | 200 mL |
| 1 US gal | 2.6 fl oz |
| 5 US gal | 12.8 fl oz |

Source: Husqvarna 450 II (litres), STIHL MS 162/172 (US gallons). Saws from other makers may want a different ratio: use the one on the saw or in its manual.

A fuel tank can be under pressure when the saw is hot, in hot weather, and especially when it is half full or more; opening it can spray fuel over you; winter-blend petrol is more volatile and makes that more likely (STIHL MS 162/172). Let the saw cool, open the cap slowly and stop if it hisses. The Forest Service guide adds: let the saw cool at least 5 minutes, fuel it on bare ground at least 6 m (20 ft) from any open flame or other source of ignition, and don't fill cans more than 90 % (USFS chain saw course ch3). OSHA's logging rule sets the minimum lower: at least 3 m (10 ft) from any open flame or ignition source, with the engine shut off, and the saw started at least 3 m (10 ft) from the fuelling area (OSHA 1910.266); that is the figure on the [Clearing a fallen tree](#guides/safety_clearing_blowdown) card. The Forest Service's 6 m is the stricter one, so use it when you can.

## Oil reaching the chain
A chain run dry ruins the bar and chain in a short time and can break (STIHL MS 162/172). Refill the oil tank every time you refuel (Oregon M&S manual). If the oil test shows no oil: check the level, then clean the oil inlet hole in the bar, the outlet on the saw and the groove (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II).
- **Never used motor oil.** STIHL warns that repeated skin contact with waste oil can cause skin cancer and that it doesn't lubricate a chain properly; Oregon says used oil carries acids and grit that wear the bar and chain (STIHL MS 162/172, Oregon M&S manual).
- **Biodegradable bar oil** must be the ageing-resistant kind, or it turns to resin that gums up the chain and can seize the oil pump (STIHL MS 162/172).
- **Winter:** below 0 °C (32 °F) some chain oils get too thick and can damage the oil pump; use an oil whose viscosity suits the air temperature (Husqvarna 450 II). Oregon's older manual agrees: for frozen wood it says to use a lighter bar-and-chain oil, and it warns that frozen wood wears the cutters fast, so touch the chain up often (Oregon M&S 2004).

## The bar
- **Turn it over** each time you sharpen or change the chain (STIHL) or daily (Husqvarna). Either way up is fine, even if the printing ends up upside down (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II).
- **Burrs:** chain wear raises a sharp lip on the outer edges of the rails. File it off with a flat file; replace the bar if the burrs can't be filed off (STIHL MS 162/172, USFS chain saw course ch3).
- **Groove:** clean it every time you file, or at least daily, because filings in it act as grinding paste (USFS chain saw course ch3). Replace the bar when the groove is too shallow for the chain to ride on the rails, or narrowed or spread (STIHL MS 162/172, USFS chain saw course ch3).
- **Uneven rails** (one worn lower) make the saw cut at an angle; truing them needs a bar grinder (USFS chain saw course ch3).
- **Blue spots** on the bar mean it overheated and went soft: replace it (USFS chain saw course ch3).
- **Nose sprocket:** it should spin freely; keep its grease hole clear and grease it (Husqvarna 450 II, USFS chain saw course ch3).
- **Not a lever:** never use the bar to lift, twist or pry (Oregon M&S manual).

## The sprocket
The drive sprocket wears grooves where the chain's drive links sit. STIHL has the sprocket replaced once those marks are deeper than 0.5 mm (0.020 in), and notes that running two chains in turn reduces sprocket wear (STIHL MS 162/172). Husqvarna's manual covers both spur sprockets welded to the clutch drum and separate rim sprockets; check whichever your saw has for wear (Husqvarna 450 II). While the cover is off, brush wood dust, resin and dirt off the chain brake and clutch drum: dirt and wear weaken the brake (Husqvarna 450 II).

## Filter, plug and cooling fins
- **Air filter:** a dirty filter causes hard starting, low power, engine wear and high fuel use (Husqvarna 450 II). Clean it the maker's way: Husqvarna brushes or shakes its filter and washes it in detergent and water; STIHL knocks its filter plate out and blows it through from the inside with compressed air; the Forest Service guide says to tap a filter clean rather than scrape it, never blow it with an air hose, and never clean it in fuel (Husqvarna 450 II, STIHL MS 162/172, USFS chain saw course ch3). Old filters can't be fully cleaned: replace them (Husqvarna 450 II).
- **Spark plug:** wrong mix (too much oil), a dirty filter and long running at part throttle leave deposits on the plug (STIHL MS 162/172). A healthy plug tip is beige and dry, not black (USFS chain saw course ch3). STIHL replaces the plug after about 100 hours or sooner if the electrodes are eroded; Husqvarna says monthly or more often (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II). Gaps vary: 0.5 mm (0.02 in) on the MS 162/172; check your model's manual (STIHL MS 162/172).
- **Cooling:** dust packed in the cylinder fins and starter intake overheats the engine. Husqvarna brushes them weekly (Husqvarna 450 II).
- **Spark arrester screen:** on a saw with a screen in the muffler, Husqvarna cleans it weekly with a steel brush, gloves on, in a ventilated area, never with compressed air, because the deposits may be carcinogenic; a blocked screen overheats the cylinder and piston, and a saw with the screen missing or not working shouldn't be run (Husqvarna 450 II).
- **Flooded engine:** take the plug out and dry it, set the switch to stop, pull the starter several times to clear the cylinder, refit the plug and start again (STIHL MS 162/172).

## Cold starts and winter running
- **Cold start:** brake on, saw on the ground with your foot in the rear handle, choke on; on saws with a primer bulb press it until fuel fills it (Husqvarna about 6 times, STIHL at least 10). Pull until the engine fires, then take the choke off and pull until it runs (Husqvarna 450 II, STIHL MS 162/172). Never drop-start a saw ([Clearing a fallen tree](#guides/safety_clearing_blowdown)).
- **Carburettor icing:** a saw that won't start, idles badly or stalls in the cold may have an iced carburettor; STIHL's fix is to let the engine warm up gradually to about 10 °C (50 °F) (STIHL MS 162/172).
- **Winter cover:** Husqvarna sells a cover that blocks part of the starter air intake below −5 °C (23 °F) or in snow, to keep the engine warm and snow out of the carburettor; take it off above −5 °C or the engine overheats (Husqvarna 450 II).

## Swapping bars and chains from other saws
A salvaged bar and chain only fit if they match the saw: the chain's pitch must match the drive sprocket and nose sprocket, the drive links must fit the groove width, the number of drive links must suit the bar length, and the bar's oil hole and tensioner hole must line up with the saw (Husqvarna 450 II). Low-kickback chains and bars matter more than speed: STIHL warns that chains made for faster cutting are more prone to kickback (STIHL MS 162/172). STIHL also warns that a bar and chain combination not listed for the saw can raise kickback forces, and Husqvarna says to use only approved combinations to keep the saw's safety functions (STIHL MS 162/172, Husqvarna 450 II). STIHL says to choose the shortest bar that does the job.

## Battery and corded saws
The bar, chain, sprocket and oiler need exactly the same care. Battery packs have temperature limits: STIHL's AK-system saws are best charged between 5 and 40 °C and used between −10 and +40 °C. STIHL warns that a pack charged or used outside −20 to +50 °C, or stored above +70 °C, may catch fire or explode (STIHL MSA 60/70). Bring cold packs into a room at 5 °C or above to charge them, on a non-combustible surface; see the [lithium fire card](#browse/hazards/li_fire) for damaged or swollen packs. A wet pack needs at least 48 hours to dry at 15–50 °C before use (STIHL MSA 60/70). On a corded saw, check the cord and plug before every use; see the [mains card](#browse/hazards/mains).

## When the chain brake fails
No dealer means no brake service. If the brake slips in the running test or fails to snap on in the inertia test after cleaning, park the saw: a brake in poor repair may stop the chain late or not at all (STIHL MS 162/172).
